You are testing one angle of PR #81 for the Zimmermann PWA Kit (a large PDP product-gallery feature: ZimmProductGallery, ZimmGalleryOverlay, ZimmMediaTile, plus colour-swatch changes). You are READ-ONLY: never edit any file, never "fix" anything — only report. Do not do any visual/Figma/browser rendering checks — that's out of scope, handled separately.

Worktrees (already checked out, do not re-clone/checkout):
- HEAD (PR tip): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-head
- BASE: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/37973080-8be5-46e1-9aab-e2abcb81ea17/scratchpad/pr81-base

Already settled: tsc clean both sides, vitest all green both sides (52 files/768 tests on head), lint debt is 100% pre-existing/unrelated. audit:tokens shows zero NEW unacknowledged violations from this PR (2 pre-existing ones are untouched files). Don't re-run these.

Read these project rule files first, they are the actual spec you're grading against: `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `.claude/rules/css.md`, `.claude/rules/components.md`, `.claude/rules/conventions.md`.

YOUR LANE: styling conformance, token hierarchy, tier ownership/Hard Rules 5&6, imports, and component/hook/story structure. Another agent covers correctness/React-logic, another covers swatch-group behavioral contract fidelity, another covers security/a11y, another covers DRY-duplication/test-coverage/story-interactivity — do not duplicate those, stay in yours.

New/changed files, all under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` in HEAD unless noted: `organisms/zimmProductGallery/` (index.tsx, .css.ts), `organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/` (index.tsx, .css.ts), `atoms/zimmMediaTile/` (index.tsx, .css.ts), `atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (index.tsx, .css.ts), `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (index.tsx, .css.ts, zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts), `atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx`, plus `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

Specific things to check — treat each as a lead to verify yourself, not a fact:

1. **Styling hierarchy (overrideStyling.md).** In every new/changed file listed above: any bare Chakra token key standing in for a `var(--zimm-*)` reference (e.g. `color="text.default"` instead of `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`)? Any raw fontSize instead of `textStyle`? Any Chakra array-shorthand responsive prop (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) where the codebase's own convention requires an explicit `@media` query instead (check `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP`/`TABLET_UP` pattern vs `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP` — are both consistent with the footer.css.ts reference pattern the rule file describes)? Any component using a bare literal instead of an already-established foundation token where one exists?

2. **Semantic intent check.** For every `var(--zimm-color-*)` used in the new files, does the semantic category match the CSS property it's applied to — `text.*`/`icon.*` on `color:`, `background.*`/`bg.*` on `background:`, `border.*` on `border-color:`? Grep for all `var(--zimm-color-` usages in the 6 new/changed component+recipe files and check each one. Flag any mismatch as should-fix and name what token *should* exist if it doesn't.

3. **Recipe state exhaustiveness.** For every new interactive part across zimmProductGallery.css.ts, zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts, zimmMediaTile.css.ts, zimmColourSwatch.css.ts (circle variant): does it define `_hover`/`_focusVisible`/`_active`/`_disabled` where a real designed state would need one? Specifically check: the `triggerOverlay` full-cover button (has `_focusVisible` — does it need `_hover`? is there a hover-affordance anywhere for "click anywhere to open gallery"?), the dot-bar buttons (`galleryDot` sx — only `_focusVisible` override, rest inherited from ZimmButton's `icon` variant — confirm that's sufficient), the gallery thumbnail buttons in zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts (`thumbnail` part — only `_focusVisible`, no `_hover` — is a hover state expected for a 102px clickable thumbnail? look for any comment addressing this one way or the other), and the circle colour-swatch variant (compare its `_focusVisible` treatment against the square variant's — is anything present in square but silently dropped in circle, or vice versa?). Where you can't tell whether a state was designed or not (no Figma node named in code comments), say so explicitly rather than assuming it's fine.

4. **Hover-gating correctness.** Is there any part in these recipes that is hidden by default and revealed only on hover/focus (a `(hover: hover)` media-capability check, or a `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` selector)? Search for `hover:` and `@media` in all the new .css.ts files. If you find one, confirm the hidden-state's own gating condition and the reveal-trigger's gating condition are the exact same real-time-interaction condition (not one keyed on device capability and the other on actual pointer/focus state). If none exists in this PR's new code, say so — this angle may be vacuous here, confirm that rather than assume it.

5. **Stacking-context / z-index lift-list completeness.** `zimmProductGallery.css.ts` defines `Z_INDEX_TRIGGER_OVERLAY=1` / `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL=2` for its "full-cover trigger vs. must-stay-clickable siblings" pattern. Grep for `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL` across the whole `overrides/` tree — I already found it independently re-declared as a local `const` in THREE separate files (zimmProductGallery.css.ts, zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts, zimmMediaTile.css.ts), each `= 2`, with no shared import — confirm this yourself with exact line numbers, and confirm whether any *new interactive element* in this PR was left OUT of the "must stay clickable above the trigger overlay" list (i.e., a part that has `cursor: pointer` or an onClick but no zIndex lift, sitting inside a container that also has a z-index-1 full-cover trigger sibling). Trace the actual DOM nesting in the corresponding .tsx files, don't just read the .css.ts in isolation.

6. **Hard Rule 5 ("never refactor upward") & Hard Rule 6 ("never rename/move a shared hook or component") re: the ZimmMediaTile extraction.** `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO` and the `mediaFallback`/`videoControlsWrapper` recipe parts moved from `zimmProductGallery.css.ts` into the new `zimmMediaTile.css.ts` (per that file's own comment). Diff `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/zimmProductGallery.css.ts` between BASE and HEAD to see exactly what was removed, and confirm ZimmProductGallery's own public contract (its exported prop types, its own recipe's remaining parts) is unaffected — i.e. this was a clean net-new extraction, not a change to an existing component's contract that some other caller depended on. Also check: was there a pre-existing `ZimmProductGallery` component in BASE at all, or is the whole organism (and this extraction) net-new in this PR? (This changes whether Hard Rule 6 is even in play.)

7. **`theme/components/index.ts` registration.** Confirm `ZimmProductGallery`, `ZimmGalleryOverlay`, `ZimmMediaTile`, and the modified `ZimmColourSwatch`/`ZimmColourSwatchGroup` recipes are all correctly imported and included in the exported `components` object (not just imported-but-unused, and not duplicated).

8. **Imports.** (a) Base-path-import check: does any new file import an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path instead of a relative path? Check `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx`'s `import DynamicImage from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/dynamic-image'` — is `dynamic-image` itself overridden anywhere in `overrides/`? (grep to confirm) — if not overridden, base path is correct per the rule; if it IS overridden, this is a real finding. (b) Check `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`'s `import { buildRelatedSwatches, type RelatedSwatch } from '../../pages/product-detail/productInfo'` — a components/-level file importing from a pages/-level file. Is this an inverted dependency direction (pages should depend on components, not vice versa)? Is there circularity risk (does `pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` import anything from `components/product-view`, even transitively)? Given `productInfo.ts`'s `buildRelatedSwatches` is now consumed by two different call sites, should it have been promoted to `overrides/app/utils/` per this repo's own DRY convention instead of staying page-nested and cross-imported? (c) General sweep: any circular imports, any `../../../..` chains deeper than 3 in the new files, any import that looks like it reaches into a later-sprint feature (check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` if it exists).

9. **Structure.** For each new component (ZimmProductGallery, ZimmGalleryOverlay, ZimmMediaTile): named export matches folder name? Props type named `<Component>Props`? Story file present? Own test file present for anything with real logic? Any data-fetching hook (SDK/React-Query) called inside a leaf component (as opposed to `useIntl`/`useUiCopy`, which are fine per the exception)?

Report format: one block per numbered item. Each finding needs file:line, what's wrong and which rule it violates, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, severity (🔴 must-fix/🟡 should-fix/🔵 note), and UNIFORM (could recur elsewhere) or ONE-OFF. End with "What I tried to falsify" and "What I could not verify" sections. If an angle is genuinely clean or vacuous for this PR, say so in one line rather than padding.

     1	import React from 'react'; // required for JSX transform in this project's tsconfig
     2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     3	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
     4	
     5	const ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_RECIPE = 'ZimmColourSwatch';
     6	
     7	// Same import base SFCC's own swatch-group/swatch.jsx uses for its `RouteLink` — a router
     8	// `Link` is what actually delivers "URL updates without a full page reload": it pushes history
     9	// rather than navigating the document. There is no overrides/.../link equivalent to reuse
    10	// instead — confirmed none exists for this.
    11	const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink);
    12	
    13	type ZimmColourSwatchProps = {
    14	  /** Colour display name. Not rendered as visible text — used as the accessible name (`aria-label`). */
    15	  name: string;
    16	  /**
    17	   * Fully resolved image URL for this colour's swatch fill. Resolution is the caller's job —
    18	   * this component performs no SFCC-shape lookup of its own.
    19	   */
    20	  imageUrl: string;
    21	  /**
    22	   * Destination URL for this colour variation. Absent for the quick-view-modal path, where
    23	   * SFCC's own `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null` and the swatch must not navigate.
    24	   */
    25	  href?: string;
    26	  /**
    27	   * When true, navigation uses a native `<a>` tag instead of a router `<Link>`, producing a
    28	   * full page reload. Required for related-colour swatches (SFCC-708), which link to a different
    29	   * master product — SPA navigation alone does not reinitialise the product fetch for a new ID.
    30	   */
    31	  forceReload?: boolean;
    32	  /**
    33	   * Selection callback for the linkless path (no `href`). Called on click and arrow-key
    34	   * navigation from the parent group. Ignored when `href` is provided — selection is handled
    35	   * by the router link in that case.
    36	   */
    37	  onClick?: () => void;
    38	  /** Whether this is the currently selected colour. */
    39	  isSelected: boolean;
    40	  /**
    41	   * Whether this swatch is reachable via Tab (`tabIndex={0}`) vs. removed from the tab order
    42	   * (`tabIndex={-1}`) — the caller drives a roving tabindex across the swatch group.
    43	   */
    44	  isFocusable: boolean;
    45	  /**
    46	   * 1-indexed position of this swatch within the full offered colour set. Together with
    47	   * `setSize`, produces correct "N of M" SR announcements even when only a page-worth of
    48	   * swatches is visually present — `overflow: hidden` can cause some AT to under-count the
    49	   * implicit set size.
    50	   */
    51	  posInSet?: number;
    52	  /** Total number of offered colours in the group. Companion to `posInSet`. */
    53	  setSize?: number;
    54	};
    55	
    56	/**
    57	 * Atom — a single colour swatch in a PDP colour-variation list: a clickable rectangle filled
    58	 * with that colour's product photo, radio semantics (one selection out of the group), and a
    59	 * router `Link` when a destination URL exists so selecting a colour updates the URL without a
    60	 * full page reload.
    61	 *
    62	 * Purely presentational — no data-fetching hook of any kind. SFCC data resolution (building
    63	 * `imageUrl`/`href` from a product's variation attributes) happens at the page level, not this
    64	 * atom.
    65	 */
    66	export const ZimmColourSwatch = ({
    67	  name,
    68	  imageUrl,
    69	  href,
    70	  onClick,
    71	  isSelected,
    72	  isFocusable,
    73	  posInSet,
    74	  setSize,
    75	  forceReload,
    76	}: ZimmColourSwatchProps) => {
    77	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_COLOUR_SWATCH_RECIPE, { selected: isSelected });
    78	
    79	  // The dynamic URL genuinely cannot live in the static recipe file, so this one dynamic `__css`
    80	  // spread is the correct, deliberate exception — the same shape already used in
    81	  // footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx, an established pattern in this codebase.
    82	  // backgroundImage is dynamic per swatch — cannot live in the static recipe file. The
    83	  // data-image-url attribute is a test hook (element.style is not populated by emotion in JSDOM).
    84	  const image = (
    85	    <chakra.span __css={styles.image} style={{ backgroundImage: `url(${imageUrl})` }} data-image-url={imageUrl} />
    86	  );
    87	
    88	  /*
    89	   * Deliberately no `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` here, unlike base SFCC's own
    90	   * `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` (product-view/index.jsx, and our own extraction of it in
    91	   * product-view/index.tsx). Three reasons this stays out, permanently, not an oversight to
    92	   * "fix" back in later:
    93	   *   1. It uses the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword — "Ivory" resolves as a
    94	   *      real CSS colour, "Bay Blue" does not — which is both unauditable by `audit:tokens` and
    95	   *      against this codebase's no-raw-design-value rule.
    96	   *   2. In base it exists to tint the swatch behind a *missing* product image. This component is
    97	   *      only ever rendered for colour variations that already have a populated image — the
    98	   *      caller filters out any variation without one before rendering this component at all —
    99	   *      so there is never a missing image for a fallback tint to show behind.
   100	   *   3. Even if one slipped through, `background-size: cover` on the image (see the recipe's
   101	   *      `image` part) would hide any tint sitting behind it regardless.
   102	   */

   104	    return (
   105	      <chakra.a
   106	        href={href}
   107	        __css={styles.swatch}
   108	        role="radio"
   109	        aria-checked={isSelected}
   110	        aria-label={name}
   111	        aria-posinset={posInSet}
   112	        aria-setsize={setSize}
   113	        tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
   114	        data-testid="colour-swatch"
   115	        onKeyDown={(e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {
   116	          // WAI-ARIA radio pattern requires Space to activate; native <a> only fires click on
   117	          // Enter. Without this handler, keyboard users pressing Space get no action.
   118	          if (e.key === ' ') {
   119	            e.preventDefault(); // prevent page scroll
   120	            window.location.href = href;
   121	          }
   122	        }}
   123	      >
   124	        {image}
   125	      </chakra.a>
   126	    );
   127	  }
   128	
   129	  if (href) {
   130	    return (
   131	      <ColourSwatchLink
   132	        to={href}
   133	        __css={styles.swatch}
   134	        role="radio"
   135	        aria-checked={isSelected}
   136	        aria-label={name}
   137	        aria-posinset={posInSet}
   138	        aria-setsize={setSize}
   139	        tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
   140	        data-testid="colour-swatch"
   141	      >
   142	        {image}
   143	      </ColourSwatchLink>
   144	    );
   145	  }
   146	
   147	  // Linkless path (quick-view): render a button so the swatch is keyboard-focusable and
   148	  // carries the same radio semantics as the href path — no navigation, selection via onClick.
   149	  return (
   150	    <chakra.button
   151	      __css={styles.swatch}
   152	      type="button"
   153	      role="radio"
   154	      aria-checked={isSelected}
   155	      aria-label={name}
   156	      aria-posinset={posInSet}
   157	      aria-setsize={setSize}
   158	      tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1}
   159	      onClick={onClick}
   160	      data-testid="colour-swatch"
   161	    >
   162	      {image}
   163	    </chakra.button>
   164	  );
   165	};
   166	
   167	export type { ZimmColourSwatchProps };
   168	export default ZimmColourSwatch;

     4	/**

     8	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.

    11	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
    12	 *
    13	 * Six parts:
    14	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
    15	 *     Capped to a fixed `maxWidth` (`GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH`, see below) unconditionally — not just
    16	 *     when paginated — so `labelName`'s truncation CSS always has a definite width to truncate
    17	 *     against. See this part's own baseStyle comment for the full explanation.

    19	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
    20	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
    21	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
    22	 *     absolute-position hack.
    23	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
    24	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
    25	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
    26	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
    27	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
    28	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
    29	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug

    31	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
    32	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).

# PR #81 Review — Styling Conformance, Tokens, Tier Ownership, Imports, Structure

## 1. Styling hierarchy (overrideStyling.md)

**Clean.** Swept all five new/changed `.css.ts` files (`zimmProductGallery.css.ts`, `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`, `zimmMediaTile.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`) plus the `.tsx` files:

- No bare Chakra token key standing in for a `var(--zimm-*)` reference anywhere — every colour/spacing value is either a `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom property or a documented `audit-allow` raw literal (`zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:15` 720px, `:104` 102px; `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:49` 47×72px — all pre-existing pattern, properly commented).
- No raw `fontSize` — the two `textStyle` usages found (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:200` `textStyle="productNames"`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:178` `textStyle="caption"`) are both correct uses of the bare-key exception the rule explicitly carves out for `textStyle`.
- No Chakra array-shorthand responsive prop anywhere (`grep` for `[base|md:|lg:|xl:` came back empty across all five recipe files) — both `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP`/`TABLET_UP` and `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP` follow the same idiom: a precomputed `` `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.X})` `` string constant, reused as a computed-property key (`[DESKTOP_UP]: {...}`). This is consistent with `footer.css.ts`'s inline `` [`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`] `` pattern (same explicit-`@media`, no-array-shorthand principle) — the only difference is precomputing the string once vs. inlining it per usage, which is a DRY improvement, not a deviation. Both gallery files are also consistent with each other.
- `zimmButton/index.tsx`'s new `sx?: SystemStyleObject` passthrough prop is the correct mechanism for the gallery components to reach `ZimmButton`'s canonical styling surface (`galleryButton`/`galleryDot` in `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`) without creating a competing `.zimm-*` global class — matches "one canonical styling surface per component type."

No findings for this item.

## 2. Semantic intent check

Grepped all `var(--zimm-color-*)` usages in the six files. All `background:`/`bg:` uses match `bg.*`/`opacity.*` categories correctly (`bg-02`, `bg-07`, and `opacity-50` for the modal scrim — confirmed the same `opacity-50` token is the established scrim colour, already used identically in `zimmModal.css.ts:13` and `zimmDrawer.css.ts:57`). All `border`-bearing properties (`borderBottom`, and the inset-`boxShadow` focus-ring idiom) correctly use `border.*` tokens.

**Finding:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:127` — `closeButton` part sets `color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'`, but this button is rendered via `<ZimmButton variant="icon" icon="close" ... />` (`index.tsx:189-197`) — an icon-only control, not text. A dedicated `--zimm-color-icon-default` token exists (`zimmTokens.ts:83`) specifically for this category, and this exact PR demonstrates correct use of the sibling `icon.*` token elsewhere: `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:201`, `pageButton`'s `_disabled` state, `color: 'var(--zimm-color-icon-disabled)'` for its ZimmIcon chevron. Using `text.default` on an icon element doesn't break the letter of the rule (the rule lists `text.*`/`icon.*` as both valid for `color:`), but it's an avoidable inconsistency against a more specific token this same PR shows awareness of.
CONFIRMED (token mismatch verified in source) / 🔵 note (doesn't violate the letter of the hierarchy rule) / ONE-OFF.

## 3. Recipe state exhaustiveness

- **`triggerOverlay` (zimmProductGallery.css.ts:139-153):** only `_focusVisible` defined. Base style sets `cursor: 'pointer'` (line 147), which is the only hover affordance present anywhere for "click anywhere to open gallery." No comment in the file confirms a visual `_hover` state was considered and deliberately excluded, unlike most other decisions in this file which cite a specific Figma node or design-team direction. UNVERIFIED-design-intent — flagging per your instruction rather than assuming it's fine. 🔵 note.
- **`galleryDot` (zimmProductGallery.css.ts:173-178):** only `_focusVisible` override, confirmed. This IS sufficient — `ZimmButton`'s shared `icon` variant recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts:150-192`) already defines `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible` for every icon-variant button, and `galleryDot`'s `sx` only needs to override `_focusVisible` (for the edge-clipping inset-shadow fix) — `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled` remain correctly inherited. CONFIRMED sufficient, no gap.
- **`thumbnail` (zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:101-115):** a 102×136px clickable button, only `_focusVisible` defined, no `_hover`. Unlike `galleryDot`/close button, this is a bespoke `chakra.button`, not routed through `ZimmButton`'s variant system — so there's no inherited hover state to fall back on. No comment addresses this one way or the other (contrast with the same file's `thumbnail` comment block at lines 96-100, which cites a specific Figma node for the aspect ratio but says nothing about hover). UNVERIFIED-design-intent, flagged explicitly. 🔵 note.
- **Circle vs. square `ZimmColourSwatch` `_focusVisible`:** compared byte-for-byte (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:26-30` circle vs. `:67-71` square) — identical (`zIndex: 1`, same outline/outlineOffset). Nothing dropped. CONFIRMED clean.
- **Adjacent finding (belongs here and cross-references item 5):** `videoControlsWrapper` (`zimmMediaTile.css.ts:17-26`) and `desktopButtonWrapper`/`compactButtonWrapper` (`zimmProductGallery.css.ts:78-87`, `:118-128`) all anchor `position: absolute; bottom: 0; right: 0` at the **same** z-index tier (`Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL = 2`). For a video item that is also the last stacked/grid cell (desktop) or the currently active compact-carousel slide (mobile/tablet) while `showGalleryButton` is true, the video's play/pause/mute controls and the "Gallery +N" button occupy the identical bottom-right corner with no z-index tiebreak beyond DOM order. This isn't an element "left out" of the clickable list (both ARE lifted) — it's two same-tier controls never coordinated positionally. CONFIRMED at the code/geometry level (both explicitly `bottom:0/right:0`, tied z-index — verified in source); PLAUSIBLE that they visually collide on a real page (would need rendering to confirm exact overlap, which is out of scope here). 🟡 should-fix / UNIFORM (recurs at both the desktop-grid last-cell and the compact-carousel paths).

## 4. Hover-gating correctness

**Vacuous — confirmed, not assumed.** Grepped `hover` across all five new/changed `.css.ts` files (`zimmProductGallery.css.ts`, `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`, `zimmMediaTile.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`) — zero matches. No `:hover`, `_hover`, or `@media (hover:` selector exists anywhere in this PR's new styling code, so there is no hidden-then-revealed-on-hover pattern to check for gating-condition consistency. This angle does not apply to this PR.

## 5. Stacking-context / z-index lift-list completeness

**Confirmed via `grep -rn` across the whole `overrides/` tree:** `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL = 2` is independently re-declared as a local `const` in exactly three files, no shared import:
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/zimmMediaTile.css.ts:12`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:17`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/zimmProductGallery.css.ts:27` (alongside `Z_INDEX_TRIGGER_OVERLAY = 1` at line 26)

This is a DRY violation per `conventions.md` ("extract to a shared utility... once the same pattern appears in two places" — here, three). Unlike `breakpoints`, which all three files correctly import from `app/theme/foundation`, there's no shared module for this feature-local z-index contract. 🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.

**Secondary finding on the same constant:** `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts` has no full-cover click-anywhere trigger (`Z_INDEX_TRIGGER_OVERLAY` doesn't exist in this file) — it's a plain modal with explicit header/body regions. Its lone use of `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL` (line 128, on `closeButton`, a flex item with no competing absolutely-positioned sibling) doesn't appear to be clearing anything real in this component. Looks like a copy-paste carryover from the trigger-overlay pattern rather than a needed value here. CONFIRMED (no competing z-index-1 element found in this file) / 🔵 note / ONE-OFF.

**DOM-nesting trace for "left out of the clickable list":** traced every `desktopItem`/`compactSlide` subtree in `index.tsx` against its sibling `triggerOverlay`. No interactive element was found with `cursor: pointer`/`onClick` but no z-index lift while sharing a z-index-1-trigger container — every genuinely new interactive part (`desktopButtonWrapper`, `dotBar`, `compactButtonWrapper`, `videoControlsWrapper`, `closeButton`) does carry `zIndex: Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL`. The real gap isn't an omission, it's the item-3/item-5 overlap described above — two lifted controls sharing one corner.

## 6. Hard Rule 5/6 re: ZimmMediaTile extraction

**Not in play — confirmed net-new.** `find` against the BASE worktree for `zimmProductGallery`/`zimmGalleryOverlay`/`zimmMediaTile` under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` returned nothing — none of these three existed in BASE at all. The entire organism/atom family is net-new in this PR. The "moved from zimmProductGallery.css.ts" comment in `zimmMediaTile.css.ts:1-6` describes internal development-time movement within this same unshipped PR, not a refactor of a previously-shipped, other-consumer-depended-on component — Hard Rule 5 ("never refactor upward") and Hard Rule 6 ("never rename/move a shared hook or component") both presuppose an existing, already-relied-upon artifact, which doesn't exist here.

Verified the extraction is clean: `zimmProductGallery.css.ts`'s current `parts` array (lines 35-50) contains no `mediaFallback`/`videoControlsWrapper`, and `index.tsx` references only `styles.*` keys that exist in that same parts array (`root`, `desktopColumn`, `desktopItem`, `desktopGrid`, `desktopGridRow`, `desktopButtonWrapper`, `compactColumn`, `compactTrack`, `compactSlide`, `dotBar`, `compactButtonWrapper`, `triggerOverlay`, `galleryButton`, `galleryDot`) — no dangling references to the extracted parts. CONFIRMED clean, no violation.

## 7. `theme/components/index.ts` registration

**Confirmed clean.** `ZimmProductGallery`, `ZimmGalleryOverlay`, `ZimmMediaTile`, `ZimmColourSwatch`, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` are each imported exactly once (`index.ts:28-32`) and included exactly once in the exported `components` object (`:62-66`). No duplicate imports, no imported-but-unused entries.

## 8. Imports

**(a) `dynamic-image` base-path import — confirmed correct, not a violation.** `grep -r` for `dynamic-image` under `overrides/` returns zero matches — it is not overridden anywhere. `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:4`'s `import DynamicImage from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/dynamic-image'` is therefore the correct call per the rule (base path is only wrong when a relative override exists to prefer instead).

**(b) `product-view/index.tsx:78` → `pages/product-detail/productInfo` — a real, new inverted dependency.** Confirmed via diff that this import is new in this PR (BASE's `product-view/index.tsx` had zero references to `productInfo`), while `productInfo.ts` itself is byte-for-byte unchanged (empty diff) — `buildRelatedSwatches` pre-dates this PR as a `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`-only helper, and this PR is what makes it a second, cross-layer consumer.
- **Direction:** genuinely inverted — a `components/`-level file now depends on a `pages/`-level file, backwards from the normal composition direction `components.md` assumes (pages compose components).
- **Circularity:** confirmed NOT circular today — `productInfo.ts` has zero imports of its own (`grep "^import"` returns nothing; it's deliberately dependency-free per its own JSDoc), so there's no cycle at present. But the layering violation is real regardless of whether a cycle currently exists.
- **Promotion to `utils/`:** `buildRelatedSwatches` is a pure, side-effect-free mapping function (matches `conventions.md`'s Utilities definition exactly) now consumed by two call sites in two different architectural layers (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1074` and `product-view/index.tsx:398`) — precisely the DRY trigger ("once the same pattern appears in two places") this repo's own convention cites for promoting to `overrides/app/utils/`. Not asserting it must move now (that's a separate refactor the author reasonably deferred rather than bundling into this PR per the Minimal Changes rule) — but the current placement is the actual conformance question worth raising.
🟡 should-fix / CONFIRMED / ONE-OFF (specific to this cross-import).

Secondary, lower-confidence note: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` is explicitly Squad-A territory per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` ("message the Squad A Lead directly before proceeding"), while `product-view/` isn't itself in that file's component list — this PR doesn't edit anything inside `pages/product-detail/`, only adds a new read-dependency on it from outside.
